BACKGROUND: When capture refuses a move the narrator's prose claimed (for example 'Kristin carries the workstation out to the truck' while the workstation is fixed), the player-visible reply still asserts the move. The tree already has ARM 'clause': RuntimeEngine appends one deterministic segment 'X has not moved.' (see `_refusal_segment`, `_refusal_names` in engine.py, and capture_record['refused']). We must MEASURE three arms against a baseline before choosing, so each arm has to be switchable.

REQUIRED CHANGE:
1. Add a `refusal_mode` keyword argument to RuntimeEngine.__init__ with values 'off' (default, today's behaviour minus the clause: nothing is added), 'clause', 'repair', 'renarrate'. Anything else raises ValueError. Gate the existing clause behaviour (normal turn path AND the pending-resume path) on mode 'clause'. In mode 'off' nothing about the reply changes and the existing tests that expect the clause must pass `refusal_mode='clause'` (edit tests/test_refused_move_clause.py accordingly; keep all its assertions).
2. bench/core.py: where RuntimeEngine is constructed (`RuntimeEngine(state, provider, capture=capture)` and the reload factory near it) pass `refusal_mode=variation.get('refusal_mode', 'off')`. Also record the mode name in the replicate telemetry next to where 'runtime' is recorded, and record per turn in the turn record whether a refusal was handled and the extra-call count (`refusal_extra_calls`). Keep it small.
3. ARM 'renarrate': after capture.after_commit reports refusals (same `refused` list, same non-hidden filter as the clause), make ONE extra narrator call through the SAME provider object the engine already uses (never a new URL, client or endpoint; this is a billed model endpoint, and the engine must make at most one extra call per turn, and zero when nothing was refused). Build the payload with `self.provider.assemble_turn_prompt(command)` if the provider has it, append to the 'user' text a clearly marked block: 'CORRECTION: <Names> cannot be moved or changed that way and did not move. Narrate the attempt as it actually ends: the player tries, and the thing stays where it was. Do not claim the move.', send it through the provider's existing request method (`_request_allowing_one_transient_retry` on CloudflareTurnProvider, or the provider's own callable if that is the only interface; read storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py to pick, and make a stub provider in tests work through the callable path), parse with parse_turn_proposal, and REPLACE only the narration/dialogue segments of the committed result with the new ones (keep entry/resolution/ending segments and all state operations untouched; commit no new facts and do not re-run capture). If the second reply fails to parse, raises, or its narration fails self.narration_validator.validate against the candidate state, fall back to the 'clause' behaviour for that turn and add an issue string 'refusal re-narration failed: <reason>'.
4. ARM 'repair': same trigger, same one-extra-call limit, same provider path, but the payload's 'user' text asks for a MINIMAL EDIT of the original reply: include the original narration text and the instruction 'Rewrite ONLY the sentences that say <Names> moved or changed so they say it stayed put. Keep every other sentence word for word. Return the same JSON shape.' Replace segments the same way and use the same fallback to the clause.
5. Shared: put the common work in small private methods (build correction payload, call once, validate, splice segments), record 'refusal clause added for <name>' style issues in delivery.capture_issues for every arm ('refusal re-narrated for <name>', 'refusal repaired for <name>'), and count extra calls in an attribute `self.refusal_extra_calls` (int, reset per turn) that bench/core.py can read.

TESTS (new tests/test_refusal_modes.py, hermetic, no network, no live worker): reuse the engine/stub setup in tests/test_refused_move_clause.py. Cases for each mode: 'off' leaves the reply unchanged; 'clause' appends the clause; 'renarrate' replaces narration with the second stub reply, calls the provider exactly twice, and leaves facts unchanged; 'repair' likewise; both fall back to the clause when the second reply is invalid or fails validation; no refusal => exactly one provider call in every mode; invalid mode raises ValueError. If a stub cannot be built as described, adapt to the nearest real behaviour and say so in notes; never weaken the call-count assertions.

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_refusal_modes.py tests/test_refused_move_clause.py tests/test_unknown_identity_not_creation.py tests/test_pipeline_eval.py tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py tests/test_bench_item_facts.py. Also run the bench-related and engine tests: `-k "bench or engine or capture or item_facts"` over tests/ and report failures. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix and -m ruff format on every file you changed. Reply with the files changed.
